Timeline Factory API Reference¶

Back to PlussQit API Reference

This reference teaches the free functions in pluss::timeline. They answer a different question from the Timeline method reference: how to create, combine, choose, or render instants before there is a receiver on which to call a method.

Choose By Intent¶

  • Parse complete timestamps with make; require date-only or clock-only input with date and time.

  • Use make_timeline only when the flat construction shortcut reads more naturally at the call site; it is an exact alias of timeline::make.

  • Preserve exact integer nanoseconds with from_epoch.

  • Build regular sequences with date_range or arange; their step and endpoint contracts differ and are documented separately.

  • Allocate known shapes with epoch, full, or full_like.

  • Sample half-open nanosecond intervals with random, or inclusive intervals with rand_between.

  • Concatenate flattened inputs with unite, and choose by ordered conditions with select.

  • Render a diagnostic representation with print, or shape-preserving text values with format.

  • Resolve fixed or relative scalar expressions with moment, now, and today.

Every deterministic output in these pages is produced by examples/CodeH/timeline_factory_reference_demo.cpp. Seeded examples make the random pages reproducible; live-clock examples state invariants rather than pretending that now() has a fixed output.

In signatures, string_range and integer_range mean any accepted contiguous range of those values; nested_string_values means a rectangular braced literal up to rank three. Those labels describe call-site concepts and intentionally do not expose the private reader adapters that implement overload unification.
